meta.title: Cheapest flight, at most one stop
meta.subtitle: A 9:16 daily-question Short (LeetCode 787, example 1)

lines.cap: Cheapest flight from 0 to 3, at most one stop.
lines.say: Cheapest flight from city zero to city three, with at most one stop.

lines.cap: 4 cities. Each arrow is a flight with its price.
lines.say: Four cities. Each arrow is a flight, with its price.

lines.cap: k = 1: at most one city in between.
lines.say: k is one. So at most one city in between.

lines.cap: What is the cheapest price from 0 to 3?
lines.say: What is the cheapest price from zero to three? Pick one.
Zero, one, two, three costs four hundred.

lines.cap: …but cities 1 and 2 are two stops. Not allowed.
lines.say: But cities one and two are two stops. Not allowed.
Zero, one, three. One stop, seven hundred.
k stops means k plus one flights.

lines.cap: Relax every flight k + 1 times, reading last round's prices.
lines.say: So relax every flight k plus one times, reading last round's prices.

lines.cap: Round 1 reaches city 1 for 100. Round 2 reaches city 3 for 700.
lines.say: Round one reaches city one for one hundred. Round two reaches city three for seven hundred.

lines.cap: Bellman-Ford, k + 1 rounds: O(k·E) time. Tomorrow: a new one.
lines.say: Bellman Ford, k plus one rounds. A new question tomorrow.
